reference_limitations: This is a source-only model item-design proposal, not audited human gold, legal certification, or an evaluation of any report.
All permitted case evidence comes from judgment-report excerpts rather than original adoption deeds, arbitral records, payment instruments, pleadings or property exhibits.
Award terms, party allegations, procedural events, lower-court findings, lower-court decrees and open appellate questions retain separate evidentiary and procedural statuses.
The replacement contains 47 independently assessable equal-weight binary items. The number follows the identified material relations rather than a target count.
Each proposed item is assessed once. Shared old_item_ids preserve provenance and do not create additional weights.

Necessary actor, property, procedural-stage, polarity and temporal-condition bindings remain within each corresponding item. Incidental numerical and identifying details do not become additional mandatory criteria.
An OPEN item's satisfaction requires recognizing its particular source-supported legal uncertainty or conditional test, not supplying an unsupported final legal outcome.
Historical reporting of the compromise, adoption declarations or estoppel finding does not establish the current legal operation of those propositions.
Relevant statutory excerpts are conditionally usable analytical sources. Their mere presence does not establish historical applicability, and unrelated supplied provisions are not mandatory.
The original reference's separate findings, defenses, future-right language, adoption priority, and remedial restrictions have been preserved without requiring the withheld target disposition.
No evaluated reports, model methods, experimental scores, hidden target reasoning, external sources or case-memory information were used.
